title: Warm limits and farewell to old words

captions.emotions: Feeling the loss of earlier words

meaning: You can combine wanting to share with a clear boundary and preserve honest agreement while acknowledging sadness for an earlier formula of complete openness.
text: Temperance in the physical position of your Vishuddha appears in joining a wish to share with a clear limit to the account. Justice in energy supports the honest scope of agreement rather than allowing extra commitment to be attributed to words. Death in emotions brings farewell to an earlier formula of openness. You can speak warmly and precisely while old simplicity still matters. A boundary does not cancel participation, and regret cannot answer for you both.

For example, an answer combines willingness to tell one important episode with a request to keep other details personal for now. You discuss this without the familiar “We have no secrets at all”. **Honest participation can have an understandable limit**. Agreement concerns the named account rather than everything connected with it. Warmth remains through sharing. Yet a beautiful formula promising simplicity without clarification may be missed; its earlier value does not make the present boundary a broken agreement.

Loss starts pressing if expanding disclosure becomes the only way to remove it. Participation and boundary then separate, while comfort at any cost replaces an honest answer. Constructive Justice helps preserve actual agreement and hear regret separately. You can recognise why old words mattered without making them a current unlimited promise; a warm exchange need not immediately restore the earlier sense of simplicity for you both.
